lens: VISUAL-GOAL critic: will the plan actually deliver 2026-level 2.5D visuals (crisp materials, realistic weather and environment, modern water and impacts) while keeping RA2's feel and readability? Are the per-class asset strategies right? Is the vertical slice defined tightly enough to judge the look early? What is missing? Checked against the dossier plus spot checks: the YRpp header list via gh api; the Vanguard formats package (GPL-3.0-or-later, pure TS, no node: imports); vera20k zsprite_shader.wgsl BUILDNGZ handling; the RA2 VM resolution whitelist.
factual_problems: The plan labels L3 ('host takes over the whole battlefield') as optional, but the Phase 3 slice cannot be built at L2. The dossier defines L2 as HD replacements composited over the upscaled original frame. Every slice item needs the host to own the whole tactical view: PBR splat terrain with a heightfield, water under ships, rain occluded by buildings, wet ground, G-buffer lighting with explosion point lights on everything. The plan understates the layer the visual goal actually needs.

The magnification math is wrong. Guest 1024x768 onto 3456x2234 is 3.375x horizontally but only 2.91x vertically, because 4:3 does not fit a ~1.55:1 panel. You get pillarboxing or a non-uniform stretch, not 'about 3.4x'. The RA2 VM whitelist (src/games/resolution.ts) offers 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x720, 1280x800, 1440x900, 1600x900 and 1920x1080, and none of them maps to this panel at an integer scale.

It is an internal inconsistency: the G2 acceptance says 'in a 1080p view with 100+ units' while the architecture and risk table assume a 1024x768 guest. The guest resolution sets the field of view, so the performance test and the HD look test will measure different things.

The hook key list (SHP name+frame, VXL name+section, TMP name+cell) and Phase 6's 'map original warhead/anim names to HD prefabs' assume every iconic effect is an SHP anim. Tesla arcs, prism and laser beams, desolator beams, YR psychic waves, particle smoke and gas, smudges, overlays and light sources are separate engine classes. YRpp has EBolt.h, LaserDrawClass.h, RadBeam.h, WaveClass.h, ParticleSystemClass.h, SmudgeClass.h, OverlayClass.h, LightSourceClass.h, SpotlightClass.h and BuildingLightClass.h (verified via gh api). SHP/VXL hooks alone will not capture them, and the RA2 VM repo has only a LaserBlit passthrough experiment.

Section 6 says real-time glTF 'naturally solves facing consistency'. Consistency yes, but the draw call carries a quantized facing. vera20k's parity renderer notes 'a rendered voxel is always exactly 1 of 32'. A glTF driven by draw-record facing will snap in 11.25° steps, which looks worse at 3x than the original sprites. Smooth rotation needs the continuous facing read from object memory plus interpolation, and the plan does not mention this.

Section 6 cites the community verdict that DLSS 5 on RA2 is 'oily/blurry' as if verified. The dossier marks it LIKELY, taken from an AI-written smzdm comment aggregation. It should carry 【较可能】, not an implied verified tag.

The plan's water spec is 'sky reflection' only, yet it presents the Adais-style images as the target. Those images show ships, bridges and buildings reflected in the water. The dossier notes mirrored SHP billboards are geometrically wrong, and only real meshes (glTF ships) can use planar reflection. The plan never states this limitation, so the target silently promises more than the design delivers.
missing: There is no runtime asset decoder on the host. RA2 VM has no MIX/SHP/VXL/HVA/TMP/PAL parsers (verified). Host-side composition therefore cannot draw fallback objects, build terrain from map data, or turn VXL into blockout meshes at runtime. The plan names cnc-formats (Rust) for the offline pipeline only.

Capture scope for non-SHP draw paths: EBolt, LaserDraw, RadBeam, Wave, ParticleSystem, Smudge, Overlay (ore, gems, walls, bridges), LightSource/Spotlight. Also per-draw state: translucency level, tint or intensity (Iron Curtain red, chrono erase, cloak/Mirage, mind-control), shadow draws, HVA frame, slope/ramp tilt, aircraft altitude and a stable object identity per record for interpolation and one-shot particle spawning.

The in-battlefield UI layer: selection brackets, health pips, veterancy chevrons, target and waypoint lines, the building placement grid, rally flags, EVA text messages, shroud edges and the cursor (VmFrame carries a separate low-res cursor bitmap). Once the host owns the tactical view these either vanish or stay as 1x pixel art on top of 3x art. They must be captured and redrawn crisp, and belong in the slice.

The sidebar and cameos in the slice. The plan keeps the original sidebar region until Phase 7, so every demo for about a year shows a blurry non-integer-scaled sidebar over ~15% of the screen. At minimum the slice needs an integer-scaled sidebar and HD cameos for the slice's units and buildings.

Asset classes missing from the Section 6 table and the slice: trees and terrain objects (a large share of the target images' look), ore and gems fields (gameplay-critical readability of value), walls and fences, lamp posts and civilian props, bridge damage states, smudges (craters and scorches already exist in game state; map them instead of adding a second decal system), debris voxels, building damaged and burning states, rubble, and deploy transitions (MCV to ConYard buildup is a glTF-to-prerendered handoff and a likely seam).

Motion quality requirements. Unit positions and scroll only update at the guest's render rate, which drops under emulation load, and at 3x each update is a 3-pixel jump. The plan has no interpolation between guest frames (vera20k already interpolates presentation), no smooth-scroll design, and no acceptance item for judder. '60 fps presentation' does not measure it.

A depth and occlusion model that unifies per-pixel depth from 3D-rendered HD assets with RA2's native Z rules (BUILDNGZ z-shapes for buildings, which vera20k reimplements in zsprite_shader.wgsl). It needs named test cases: infantry walking behind and in front of an HD building, a vehicle under a bridge, aircraft over buildings, and a ship at a shoreline cliff.

Terrain fidelity rules. The heightfield must reproduce RA2's exact discrete ramp geometry, or units placed by the guest will float or sink. Water, shore and land-material splat weights must be per-pixel masks derived from the original TMP art. Cell land types alone give diamond-stepped shorelines and blobby transitions, and lose RA2's painted road, pavement and LAT layout. Cliffs need a decision too: a modular kit modeled after the original cliff tiles, or generic triplanar rock.

A night variant of the slice map (changing [Lighting]). It is the cheapest test of emissive windows, lamps, muzzle flashes and explosion lights, which is where relit 2.5D either shines or fails, and one of the three target scenes is a rainy night.

An art bible with numbers, written before asset production. It should fix: camera (ortho 2:1, yaw 45°, pitch 30°); a sun vector locked to the original's screen-left light; exposure; per-theater LUTs; house-color swatches with a ΔE tolerance after tone mapping; texel density; bloom threshold; caps on shake and HDR flashes; rim or outline rules for units against busy HD terrain; and a VFX intensity ceiling. The 'canon rule' alone is not measurable.

Calibration of map [Lighting] to the PBR sun and ambient. Those values are palette-domain Ambient/Level/RGB numbers, not physical intensities. Without a fitted mapping, checked by comparing Classic and HD frames of the same scene for mean luminance and hue per theater, every map's mood will drift.

A tone-mapping decision that protects house colors. AgX desaturates bright saturated colors, and that is the muted Adais look the research says hurts readability. The plan should test Neutral against AgX on team-color swatches and possibly composite team-color mask pixels to keep their hue.

Supervision and review tooling: a split-screen or wipe Classic|HD view (not only a toggle key); an HD-coverage heatmap showing which on-screen objects are still fallback; G-buffer debug views; golden save files (RA2 VM supports save/load) as fixed review scenes captured automatically every week; and a shimmer/flicker metric for scrolling and for AI-derived normal/depth across animation frames.

Readability gate details: a blind identification test (for example ≥95% of 20 random unit crops identified), repeated in late-battle clutter with smoke and explosions, under rain and night, and in grayscale. Also click alignment: visible HD pixels must stay inside the guest's selection area, because clicks still go to the original exe. And FLH alignment: muzzle, barrel-tip, tesla-coil and prism-tip positions on HD models must match art.ini FLH offsets per facing, or game-spawned flashes, bolts and projectiles will start off the barrel.

A rule for decorative weather against gameplay signals. Random decorative lightning can be mistaken for the Weather Control superweapon (which has its own IonLighting state), and decorative fog or night darkness changes what a player can see in a game with no fog of war. Decorative lightning should be banned or clearly styled differently, and density and darkness capped.

A decision point on who produces hero art. Scripted Blender cleanup of AI 3D output (about 1 in 10 usable per the dossier) is not Lemon Sky quality. The user should choose between AI-grade assets, commissioning a human 3D artist for heroes, or community models (C&C Blender Forge is unverified), with budget.
overpromises_or_risks: Progressive replacement over the upscaled guest frame will look like a patchwork. Fallback objects made from 1x-derived pixels sit next to 3-4x assets. Depth edges from a 1x guest Z-buffer upsampled to 3x produce stair-steps and halos on rain occlusion, AO and fog. If the host replaces terrain, fallback objects' shadows, which RA2 draws by darkening the terrain pixels underneath, have nothing to darken and are lost. 'Always a complete playable game' is true for gameplay, not for looks.

The Phase 2 L1 step, a water shader overlaid on water cells of the final frame, will paint over ships, bridges and splashes, and double up with the painted animated water tiles unless it is masked per pixel by object coverage. As a first visual demo it risks looking worse than Classic.

Visual judgment comes too late. The Phase 2 spike deliberately uses temporary assets (plumbing only), so the first frame at target quality arrives at the end of Phase 3, about 4-6 months in. That conflicts with a user who wants to supervise every step, and asset-throughput reality (hours per hero asset) is not measured until then.

The 2-4 month slice is optimistic. It includes about 15 final hero assets (glTF vehicles, 3D-rebuilt prerendered buildings with all channels, rigged infantry at 8 facings with exact frame parity), a full terrain rebuild, water, rain, a VFX kit, the full post chain and the unfinished L3 bridge. Estimates of 1-2 person-days per vehicle and 2-4 per building are inference with no measurement.

ChatGPT Images 2.5 paint-overs will show things the runtime cannot do: unique non-tiling detail, cinematic scale, reflections of sprites, bespoke per-shot lighting. The user may approve an unreachable target. Each target image needs original sprite outlines overlaid for scale, and each element tagged with the pipeline item that delivers it.

Terrain made from '~8 generic PBR splats per theater plus triplanar cliffs' risks a generic 3D-strategy-game look that erases RA2's hand-painted character, which the research says players miss (画风 over 画质). The urban theater (roads, sidewalks, markings) will not fit 8 splats at all.

Infantry from 'one 3D base body per faction plus ~15 retargeted motion sets' undersells the work. RA2 infantry are distinct designs (Tanya, Boris, Yuri, Desolator, Chrono Legionnaire, Crazy Ivan). Each sequence must match the original frame counts, key poses and FLH timing exactly for the draw-hook frame mapping and the Classic/HD toggle.

Mixed shadow types need matching softness, density and color, or buildings and vehicles will look lit by different suns: baked or softened shadows from prerendered buildings and infantry, real shadow maps from glTF vehicles, and fallback SHP shadow frames.
Screen shake, heat distortion and HDR flashes on the XDR display hurt RTS control and readability if not capped. The plan lists shake for the slice's ordinary tank hits and building deaths.

The WebGL2 'Medium' tier loses compute (1-D transform-feedback emulation only, no storage textures), so GPU rain, snow and compute water need a non-compute path. Otherwise the fallback tier looks much worse than the demos.

The user is an early-RA2 fan, and the RA2 1.006 campaigns (game.exe) stay Classic-only 'for a long time'. That is a major expectation risk for the visual goal. Say plainly that the HD asset work is exe-independent and reusable once a game.exe bridge exists.
The L0 filter demo shown 'the same day' can anchor the user's impression of HD toward the 'oily' AI-filter look. It should be presented explicitly as a throwaway baseline, not the direction.
efficiency_improvements: Make RenderState a stable, versioned contract and build the HD renderer first against a 'diorama harness': a static or scripted scene built from the user's map file (parsed on the host) plus placed objects. Look-dev can then start in Phase 0/1, in parallel with G1/G2 and independent of which base wins. The same renderer is reused if the project falls back to vera20k.

Reuse Vanguard's packages/formats (GPL-3.0-or-later, pure TypeScript, no node: imports — verified; covers mix, shp, tmp, vxl, pal, csf, ini, map, aud) as the host runtime decoder and in the offline pipeline. The license is compatible with RA2 VM's GPL-3.0-or-later. Its CPU voxel renderer and renderScale HD hook are working references. Keep cnc-formats only as a cross-check.

Use vera20k as a verified reference for RA2 depth semantics (native Z, BUILDNGZ z-shape in zsprite_shader.wgsl) and for presentation-side interpolation. Do not rediscover these from the exe. Its GPL-3.0-only license is fine as a reference and compatible if code is borrowed.

Pick a guest resolution that is an exact integer fraction of the panel: 1152x744 at 3x gives 3456x2232 and fills the screen (to verify in Phase 0 that the shim and RA2 accept it). Emulation cost is similar to 1024x768, fallback and UI pixels stay crisp, and the runtime density becomes 3x. Masters can still be made at 4x for future zoom or external displays.

Use golden save files (a slice-map base by day, the same in rain, night, a naval shoreline, a late battle with 100+ units) as fixed review fixtures, with automated Classic/HD/wipe screenshots every week, so the user compares the same frames each time and regressions are obvious.

Produce one hero asset end to end, for example a Grizzly (VXL blockout → AI 3D → Blender → glTF with house-color mask → in-engine under the locked sun), during the look gate. That measures real hours per asset before committing to the Phase 3/4 schedules and the human-artist decision.

Derive per-pixel water, shore and terrain-material masks automatically from the original TMP art (classify palette colors per pixel, then upscale and smooth). This beats hand-painting splat layouts, keeps RA2's layout, and gives JFA foam an accurate shoreline.

For the long tail of infantry, do a low-denoise ControlNet repaint of the original frames, pinned to their silhouettes. It stays frame-exact for the hook mapping and is far cheaper than rigging 3D for each unique infantry type. Reserve 3D for about 6 hero infantry.

Generate the ChatGPT target images from screenshots of the exact slice map and golden-save viewports, at the real display size (for example 3456x2240, which is within the 2.5 API limits), with original outlines overlaid. The target, the slice and the final comparison are then the same scene, with no snow or night targets that the slice cannot answer.

Add a small CI validator that runs on every asset: silhouette IoU against the original at each facing, house-color ΔE after the tone-map/LUT chain, footprint and click-box containment, and FLH marker alignment. The user then reviews only assets that already pass the objective gates.
must_change: Restate the HD architecture. In HD mode the host composes the entire tactical view from captured game state and draw records: host-decoded original assets as the fallback, HD assets where available, one depth, lighting and weather model. Keep the guest frame only for Classic mode and the sidebar. Drop 'HD objects over an upscaled guest frame' for terrain, water and weather. L3-lite is the core of step 2, not an option. Redefine G2 to prove this (host-drawn tactical view matching the Classic frame, then two HD swaps), not just two sprites over the guest frame.

Add a separate early look gate (G-Look) around weeks 3-6, decoupled from G2 and G1. Using the diorama harness, render one fixed screen of the slice map at the locked camera and sun with: one final-quality hero vehicle, one final-quality building, an HD terrain patch with per-pixel shoreline, water with foam and a moving ship wake, rain on wet ground, and one explosion with a point light. Show it Classic|HD split, by day and by night. The user signs off here before the slice begins.

Tighten the vertical slice definition. List 4-5 golden-save scenes. Extend the asset list with trees, ore and gems, a bridge with a damage state, MCV deploy to ConYard buildup, harvester docking, smudges, damaged and burning building states, in-tactical UI (selection, pips, placement grid, target lines, cursor, shroud edge) and slice cameos plus an integer-scaled sidebar. Require zero fallback objects in the golden scenes. Make the Phase 2 target images of those exact scenes, not unrelated snow and night cities.

Expand the capture spec explicitly to cover: EBolt, LaserDraw, RadBeam, Wave, ParticleSystem, Smudge, Overlay and LightSource draws; per-draw translucency, tint and state flags; object identity and continuous facing, turret facing, slope tilt, HVA frame and altitude. Add motion interpolation and smooth scrolling as a stated requirement, with a judder acceptance test under late-game emulation load.

Fix the resolution math and choose an integer-scaled guest resolution (proposed 1152x744 at 3x, to verify in Phase 0). Restate the density decision (D5) as 3x runtime with optional 4x masters, and make G2 performance and look tests use the same guest resolution.

Write a numeric art bible before any asset production. Add: calibration of map [Lighting] to HD lighting against Classic frames; a house-color protection test (Neutral vs AgX); caps on shake, HDR and bloom; and rules for decorative weather (no decorative lightning that mimics the Weather Storm, capped fog and darkness).

Extend the readability gate: blind identification ≥95% at default view, in late-battle clutter, under rain and night, and in grayscale; plus click-box containment and FLH muzzle alignment per facing. Add a depth/occlusion test list (behind and in front of buildings, under bridges, aircraft over structures, ships at cliffs).

Specify the terrain approach: exact RA2 ramp geometry for the heightfield, per-pixel material and water masks derived from the original TMP art, a cliff kit modeled on the original cliffs, and a statement that water reflections cover sky plus mesh objects only (not sprites). Tell the user explicitly where the 2.5D runtime cannot match the AI concept images.

Add to the decisions list who makes the hero art (AI-grade vs a human 3D artist vs community models) and the budget, and make the plan show that asset throughput is measured at the look gate before the Phase 3/4 durations are trusted.
